name: Exodus and Wilderness Wandering

objectives.text: Retell how God protected baby Moses in a basket on the Nile and raised him up to lead His people
Identify the pillar of cloud and fire as the way God led Israel and stayed with them
Retell how God parted the Red Sea to rescue Israel from Pharaoh's army
Describe how God provided manna, quail, and water for Israel in the wilderness
Recite the Ten Commandments in order as the law God gave at Mount Sinai
Retell God's call of Moses at the burning bush and explain what God revealed by the name I AM
Sequence the main events of Exodus from Israel's slavery in Egypt to their arrival at Mount Sinai
Summarize the ten plagues and explain from Exodus that God sent them to show He is the LORD over Pharaoh and the gods of Egypt
Identify what the Song of Moses praises about God after the Red Sea crossing
Explain the parts of the Passover meal and why God commanded Israel to remember it every year
Explain how the preface to the Ten Commandments grounds Israel's obedience in God's act of rescue
Compare the Golden Calf incident with the worship God commanded, using the second commandment
Explain how Moses' intercession and God's description of Himself show both His mercy and His justice
Explain how Israel's grumbling in the wilderness revealed unbelief in God's promises and provision
Identify the main furnishings of the Tabernacle and explain the purpose of each
Explain the covenant God made with Israel at Sinai and their calling to be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation
Explain how the New Testament presents Jesus as the true Passover lamb and the true bread from heaven
Analyze the passages that describe Pharaoh hardening his own heart and God hardening Pharaoh's heart
Explain why Moses was not permitted to enter Canaan after striking the rock at Meribah
Describe the main Levitical sacrifices and the Day of Atonement and explain what they taught Israel about sin and forgiveness
Connect the spies' report and Israel's rebellion at Kadesh Barnea to the forty years of wandering
Interpret the symbolism of the Tabernacle and the high priest's garments in light of the Book of Hebrews
Explain how Jesus uses the bronze serpent in the wilderness to describe His own saving work
Explain the theme of holiness in Leviticus as God dwelling among a people He has set apart
Summarize Deuteronomy as Moses' covenant renewal speeches to the new generation on the plains of Moab, including the Shema
Construct a map tracing the likely route from Egypt through Sinai to the plains of Moab with key sites labeled
Distinguish the moral, ceremonial, and judicial laws as the Reformed tradition classifies them and explain how each applies after Christ
Evaluate the early and late date theories for the Exodus using biblical and archaeological evidence
Defend the Mosaic Law as a reflection of God's holy character rather than a set of arbitrary rules
Analyze how Hebrews uses the wilderness generation to warn and exhort the church
Write an essay tracing Exodus typology through Scripture as a pattern of redemption fulfilled in Christ

changes: I kept and reworded the real competencies: Moses' birth, the Red Sea, the Ten Commandments, manna, the plagues, Passover, the Golden Calf, the Tabernacle, Pharaoh's hardening, the Tabernacle symbolism, Kadesh Barnea, Levitical holiness, the route map, the Exodus date, the defense of the law, and the typology essay. I sharpened vague verbs like Observe and Categorize into assessable tasks. I added missing content: the pillar of cloud, the burning bush and the divine name, sequencing the narrative, the Song of Moses, the preface to the commandments, Moses' intercession and Exodus 34:6-7, wilderness grumbling, the Sinai covenant, Christ as Passover lamb and bread from heaven, Moses at Meribah, the sacrifices and Day of Atonement, the bronze serpent, Deuteronomy and the Shema, the threefold division of the law, and Hebrews' use of the wilderness generation. I replaced whole-chapter references with verse ranges. I dropped Westminster Confession 8.4 as not fitting and anchored the objectives in WCF 2.1, 5.6, 7.5 and chapter 19, along with relevant Shorter Catechism and Heidelberg questions.
